Source contracts: setup.py

setup.py

Python · Tier B

Compile prompt resources, verify legal bytes and package the branding default.

Usage

Used by setuptools when building Python modules for a distribution.

Inputs

Setuptools build_py/sdist options, canonical legal documents, the packaged legal manifest and root branding.json; dependency metadata remains in pyproject.toml.

Side effects

Source builds check legal synchronization without rewriting terms. BuildPy verifies packaged hashes and available canonical bytes before copying modules, then writes agent_runtime/branding.json inside build_lib. Wheels and source archives compile the prompt catalog in staging without modifying the checkout. Archive builds tolerate the absent build/config legal sources while retaining manifest hash checks.

Cleanup

Build ownership and cleanup remain with setuptools; no runtime service is launched.

@see branding.json

@see pyproject.toml

@see src/agent_runtime/branding.py

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
check_source_legal 31 Validate source legal synchronization when the maintained build tool is present. Source archives may omit build/; their packaged-resource checks run separately in BuildPy. The temporary import path is removed even when validation fails.
compile_prompt_catalog 48 Validate authored prompts and generate distribution data without changing source.
Sdist 63 Reject an out-of-sync source legal bundle before setuptools assembles the archive.
Sdist.run 66 Check canonical resources, then retain setuptools' normal source-archive behavior.
Sdist.make_release_tree 71 Compile inside the archive tree; atomic replacement preserves source hardlinks.
BuildPy 77 Verify immutable legal bytes before copying modules and the branding resource.
BuildPy.run 80 Fail on hash/source mismatches; write branding only after the normal module build.
